Security forces kill 3 terrorists in DI Khan IBO: state media. Security forces on Monday killed three terrorists during an intelligence-based operation in the Dera Ismail Khan district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, state media reported on Monday. President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif commended the security forces for conducting the security operation. In separate statements, President Zardari said effective operations by the security forces were playing an important role in weakening terrorist networks, adding that the “nefarious designs” of terrorist elements operating with external support would be thwarted at all costs. The prime minister reiterated that the state remained committed to completely eliminating Fitna al-Khawarij . The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. The province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS). A day earlier, security forces killed eight terrorists , including three key commanders, during an IBO in DI Khan district. On September 30, security forces killed three terrorists in an IBO in KP’s Mir Ali. A day before that, in an IBO in KP’s Bara area, security forces killed five terrorists. On Monday, four terrorists were killed during an IBO in Dera Ismail Khan. Earlier, a dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured in a suicide blast that targeted the Aman Mela police checkpost in DI Khan’s Darazinda tehsil. On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation . On Sept 17, security forces killed 10 terrorists in separate operations in KP between Sept 15 and 17. Earlier in the month, over 20 terrorists were killed during multiple engagements in KP between Sept 3 and 5.

ATC directs authorities to produce PTI founder Imran Khan at next hearing in FJC attack case. ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Monday directed authorities to produce PTI founder Imran Khan before the court at the next hearing, either physically or via video link, in a case pertaining to the attack on the Federal Judicial Complex (FJC) in March 2023. ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra issued the direction while hearing the case registered against the PTI founder and other party leaders at Ramna Police Station. The court also declared former federal ministers Farrukh Habib, Hammad Azhar and Murad Saeed, and former senator Shibli Faraz, proclaimed offenders after they failed to appear before the court. The judge directed the relevant authorities to submit details of the assets owned by the proclaimed offenders. The court also issued non-bailable arrest warrants for former Punjab Assembly deputy speaker Wasiq Qayyum and PTI MPA Hassan Khan Niazi. During the proceedings, the court ordered that the PTI founder be produced before it at the next hearing, either in person or through video link. After taking up the matter, the court adjourned further proceedings until Nov 5. On March 18, 2023, clashes occurred between police and PTI workers amid Imran’s appearance at the FJC in a hearing for the Toshakhana case. The Islamabad police alleged that party workers had shelled the Judicial Complex and set fire to a police post. In turn, the PTI also accused the police of shelling Imran’s vehicle.

Ex-prince Andrew asks court to 'quash' Epstein affair search warrants. Britain’s disgraced former prince , Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, has launched a High Court challenge “to quash search warrants” obtained by police ahead of his arrest earlier this year, the judiciary confirmed Monday. The London court is set to hold a private hearing on Thursday, the judiciary said in a statement, as King Charles III’s brother challenges Thames Valley Police over searches of his former and current homes on royal estates. The force arrested the 66-year-old on his birthday on February 19 on suspicion of misconduct in public office related to his links to late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. He was released later that day while remaining under investigation. The ex-prince has denied all wrongdoing. Officers, who swooped on the remote Sandringham royal estate in eastern England to detain Andrew, searched both his home there and his former Royal Lodge residence in Windsor, west of London. The Daily Telegraph was the first to report the legal challenge by Andrew, late on Sunday. The newspaper noted it was the first time a member of Britain’s royal family has challenged the lawfulness of criminal proceedings against them since the trial of Charles I in 1649. It said his legal team wanted to examine whether the search warrants granted by a judge sitting at London’s Old Bailey court — formally known as the Central Criminal Court — were lawful. Andrew’s legal team did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The judiciary’s press office said “the case concerns an application by Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor for a judicial review to quash search warrants issued by a judge at the Central Criminal Court on 18 February 2026”. It added Thursday’s hearing concerned an application by Thames Valley Police to restrict access to court documents in the matter. The police force said in a statement: “Whilst our investigation into misconduct in public office continues, we are engaged in legal proceedings in relation to warrants previously obtained from the Central Criminal Court. “As these legal proceedings are currently ongoing, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further.” Andrew’s arrest and the police searches marked a new low-point for the disgraced ex-prince, who was stripped of his royal titles last year over his connections to Epstein. New revelations from documents relating to the American financier released by the United States earlier this year included emails in which Andrew appeared to share potentially confidential information with him.

UN chief's visit this week to highlight Pakistan's efforts towards multilateralism: FO. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres is set to visit Pakistan from Oct 6 to 8, the Foreign Office (FO) said, noting that his engagements here would highlight Islamabad’s efforts towards strengthening multilateralism. The visit comes as Guterres’ 10-year tenure as the UN chief is set to end on Dec 31. Guterres is set to meet President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, as well as Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, FO said on Monday. The statement added that the UN chief would visit the headquarters of the UN Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP) and attend a briefing at the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) headquarters. FO noted that during Guterres’s visit, Pakistan’s “efforts towards strengthening multilateralism and international peace and security, as well as its strides towards disaster preparedness and early warning, will be highlighted”. It stated that the visit will offer an important opportunity to reiterate Pakistan’s longstanding cooperation with the UN, and to exchange views on regional and international developments. In its statement, FO acknowledged Guterres’ leadership and contribution to international peace and development while serving as the UN head. FO also highlighted “Pakistan’s unwavering support for multilateralism with UN at its core, and its abiding commitment to the purposes and principles of the UN Charter”. On Friday, DPM Dar had hinted at Guterres’s visit , saying that the Pakistani delegation had met him at the UN General Assembly (UNGA) session, held in New York in September. Dar said that he had extended an invitation to Guterres to visit Pakistan, which the UN chief had accepted. PM Shehbaz had also met Guterres on the sidelines of the UNGA, with the two discussing major regional and international developments, including the situation in the Middle East. In that meeting, Guterres commended Pakistan’s role and strong voice at the UN, as well as its contribution to international peace and security. The UN chief also appreciated Pakistan’s role and sacrifices in countering terrorism. Guterres’ first visit to Pakistan as the UN secretary general was in February 2020, about three years after he was elected to the position in 2016. In recent months, two of the six candidates vying to succeed Guterres have visited Pakistan and met PM Shehbaz. During their separate meetings in July and September, respectively, María Fernanda Espinosa and Ambassador Olara Otunnu praised Pakistan’s role in efforts to promote peace.

Imaan and Hadi's arrest: ATC judge irked over IO's absence, failure to present case record. ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Monday expressed strong displeasure over the absence of the investigating officer (IO) and the police’s failure to produce the case record during the hearing of bail petitions filed by lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha in a protest-related case. ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain summoned the deputy superintendent of police (DSP) and the Judicial Complex’s security head after being informed that the IO was out of town. At the outset of the hearing, the judge repeatedly questioned DSP Legal Naeem Yousuf about the whereabouts of the IO and the case record, directing him to provide documentary evidence instead of making verbal assertions. The DSP initially informed the court that, to the best of his knowledge, the IO was out of town. The judge expressed displeasure, saying he did not appreciate mere verbal statements. The court subsequently directed the police officer to produce evidence regarding the IO’s whereabouts. The DSP later told the court that the IO was in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and produced a printout of a WhatsApp message in support of his claim. The judge refused to accept the printout and ordered the police official to produce the original document. DSP Yousuf then said the IO’s mobile phone was switched off and that it could take 10 to 15 days to establish contact with him. The judge warned that if the required record was not produced, he could send both the DSP and the superintendent of police (SP) to jail for six months. “You ought to be ashamed; you people have turned this into a display of high-handedness,” the judge remarked, questioning the manner in which the investigation was being handled. At one point, the court ordered handcuffs to be brought into the courtroom and summoned the security head. The judge also directed the security official not to allow the DSP to leave the court premises without permission and indicated that he could be arrested if he failed to provide accurate information. The judge criticised the absence of an effective judicial enforcement mechanism, observing that the same old system dating back to 1898 and 1860 was still in place. During the hearing, defence counsel Riasat Ali Azad argued that, except for the terrorism provision, all other sections incorporated in the first information report (FIR) were bailable. He said the court had already rejected the request for Imaan and Hadi’s physical remand and that there was no justification for delaying the bail proceedings merely because the IO was unavailable. “If the court requires detailed arguments, I am ready to present them,” Azad said. He alleged that the authorities had made a mockery of the judicial process by failing to produce the investigation record. Advocate Zafar Khokhar also objected to the IO taking the record away with him. The prosecution side maintained that the investigation record was not available because of the IO’s absence. The judge said he was dictating a detailed order regarding the IO’s unavailability. Subsequently, the hearing was adjourned until Oct 13. Imaan and Hadi’s rearrest The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court (IHC) and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association (IHCBA) president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial. Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case pertaining to controversial social media posts. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts . On Sept 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the Supreme Court suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the Islamabad High Court’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision. However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an ATC, which sent them to jail on judicial remand. The fresh case in which the two were arrested was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio. Imaan and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added. The FIR included sections 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), 341 (wrongful restraint), 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

Lahore police granted further four-day physical remand of 2 suspects in Azeri woman rape case. LAHORE: A judicial magistrate at the Cantonment Courts on Monday granted Lahore police a further four-day physical remand of two prime suspects in the alleged gang-rape of an Azeri woman. The 20-year-old Azerbaijan national had travelled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society near Raiwind on the night between September 25 and Sept 26. Police apprehended two of the three men, who were sent on a six-day physical remand on Sept 29. As the six-day remand period expired on Monday, the suspects were produced before Judicial Magistrate Azhar Mahmood. The investigating officer told the court that the investigation was still underway; therefore, further physical remand was required. The magistrate granted the request and extended the physical remand of both suspects by four days. He directed the police to produce the suspects again on Oct 9. Earlier, a sessions court extended the interim pre-arrest bail of a female suspect in the alleged gang-rape case. The suspect appeared before the court on Monday at the expiry of her bail period. The woman, one of the two female suspects accused of facilitating the alleged act, had secured pre-arrest bail till October 5 on Sept 29. Additional District and Sessions Judge Rafaqat Ali extended the pre-arrest bail of the woman until Oct 13. The court asked whether the investigation was complete, to which a police official said the police needed more time. In her statement , the complainant had named two women with whom she had met before the men accused of raping her gathered at an apartment. The other woman was sent on a three-day physical remand last week; however, on Saturday, at the end of her physical remand, the court sent her on judicial remand for 14 days till Oct 17. Survivor’s statement The Defence C police had registered a first information report (FIR) against three unidentified suspects on Sept 26 on the Azeri woman’s complaint. In her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) , the survivor said she had arrived in Islamabad from Istanbul on Sept 13 and stayed in Faisalabad for five days before travelling to Lahore. “I had a plan to visit Skardu, but I could not go there because I was alone,” she said. According to her, on the day of the alleged incident, she messaged two women, asking them to meet her in Lahore. At around 11pm, she went to a cafe where she met one of them — the woman sent on judicial remand — and later accompanied her to a house in Bahria Town to meet the other, who secured pre-arrest bail on Monday. The complainant told the magistrate that at around 2am, a white car arrived carrying two men, one of whom was sent on remand last week (first suspect). Later, they moved to an apartment where two more men arrived, one of whom was the second person sent on remand (second suspect), while she did not know the name of the other man. According to the complainant, in a separate room, the woman on bail took between Rs20,000 and Rs30,000 from the first suspect, saying the money was for a party, while the woman on judicial remand also joined them. The Azeri woman said she made it clear that she “did not need money or alcohol”. She alleged that the first suspect tried to touch her and locked her in a separate room. When she asked about her friends, she was told that they had left. When she tried to leave, the complainant said she was told that she could not go because her friends had taken money. The victim said she offered to pay the men, but they told her that she would have to drink alcohol with them before they would let her go. She alleged that the three men raped her. She further stated that the suspects then put her in a car and threw her out at an unknown location, while threatening her with dire consequences if she approached the police. According to her statement, the suspects also took her handbag containing Rs200,000, an iPhone 13 Pro Max and another mobile phone. She then requested some people present there to help her call the police emergency number 15, following which the police arrived. It is the second such case in which a foreign woman was reportedly gang-raped in the Defence C police station area during the last four months. In June, two foreign women, nationals of the Netherlands and Venezuela, were allegedly abducted and sexually assaulted in the Defence C police station area. According to the FIR, the women were abducted by five suspects, including a close relative of a senior political personality, who demanded ransom and subjected them to sexual assault during their captivity.

Child safety online. PAKISTANI children are spending more of their lives online, but the safeguards around them are not keeping pace. A recent Kaspersky survey covering the Middle East, Turkiye, and Africa region, including Pakistan, found YouTube to be the most popular mobile app among children surveyed here, followed by Instagram and WhatsApp. The more important issue, however, is what children may face once they are online. Multiplayer games and communication platforms can put young users in direct contact with strangers. This can expose them to grooming, fraud, blackmail, and other forms of abuse. Generative AI has made the problem more complicated. Photos and videos shared online can now be altered into convincing fake images or clips and used for cyberbullying or harassment. The survey figures should not be treated as a complete picture of all Pakistani children, but the risks it highlights are serious. The problem is that while these dangers are growing, the state’s ability to respond remains unclear. The PTA has told the Islamabad High Court that it does not have the legal authority to impose mandatory age checks or stop children under 16 from using social media. This should lead to a wider debate about how Pakistan protects children online. The answer cannot simply be to demand restrictions that a regulator may not have the power or technical means to enforce. The PTA has also noted that because major platforms use HTTPS encryption, regulators may be unable to block one harmful page or post without affecting access to the entire platform. At the same time, the 2025 amendments to Peca provide for a new ‘Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority’, raising questions about which body will ultimately be responsible and what powers it will have. Whatever system is put in place, it must go beyond blocking websites and apps. Social media platforms should be required to make children’s accounts safer, offer simple reporting tools, and respond quickly to grooming, fake content, and abuse. Any age-checking system must also protect privacy. Schools should teach children how to recognise online risks, while parents need to talk openly with them about strangers, personal information, and troubling online conversations. No single ban, parental control setting, or awareness campaign will be enough. Protecting children online will require clear laws, responsible technology companies, better digital education, and informed parents working together. Published in Dawn, October 5th, 2026

German, US scientists win Nobel prize for work that has helped understand how the brain works. American Karl Deisseroth and Germans Peter ​Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine on Monday for their discoveries on light and optogenetics ‌that have helped understand how the brain works. The Nobel Assembly of Sweden’s Karolinska Institute medical university said Deisseroth, 54, Hegemann, 71, and Nagel, 73, were selected for their “discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics”. Optogenetics “makes it possible to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells in a living brain”, said Thomas Perlmann, Secretary-General of the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet. “This ​method is now being used in laboratories around the world to reveal the brain’s mysteries,” Perlmann said. In clinical trials, researchers are restoring vision to ​people blinded by a condition called retinitis pigmentosa by inserting a light-sensitive protein in the retina. Researchers also hope optogenetics could ⁠improve cochlea implants, allowing more precise stimulation of the auditory nerve than current electrical devices. The physiology or medicine prize traditionally opens the annual Nobel announcements, with awards ​in physics, chemistry, literature, peace and economics to follow over the coming days. Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel will share a prize sum amounting to 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2m). Recipients surprised and delighted In the early 1990s, Hegemann investigated how the alga Chlamydomonas reacts to light in half a millisecond. He hypothesised that a single protein captured light and acted as an ion channel. Nagel tested this by injecting Chlamydomonas genes into frog eggs, discovering channelrhodopsin-2—an ion channel that opens when exposed to light. In 2003, they published that this protein could ​be introduced into human and hamster cells to generate electrical impulses using light. In 2005, Deisseroth at Stanford demonstrated the technique in rat nerve cells and ​the method was named optogenetics a year later. Perlmann said he had talked to all three laureates this morning, and that they were surprised and delighted. “All three said the same thing, ‌that they ⁠thought it was absolutely wonderful to receive the prize with the other two and they call them my friends. That it’s such an honour to receive them together. So that’s something they conveyed,” Perlmann said. Nobel prizes awarded since 1901 The five original Nobel Prizes were created under the terms of Swedish inventor and industrialist Alfred Nobel’s will and have been awarded since 1901, with only limited interruptions, chiefly during World War One and World War Two. A sixth award, the economics prize, was established ​in 1968 by Sweden’s central bank, ​the Riksbank. The medicine prize has honoured ⁠some of the most influential scientific discoveries of the past century, including Alexander Fleming’s work on penicillin, recognised in 1945, and Karl Landsteiner, who won in 1930 for his discovery of human blood groups. Last year, American scientists Mary Brunkow and Fred ​Ramsdell and Japan’s Shimon Sakaguchi won the prize for work shedding light on how the immune system spares healthy cells, ​creating openings for possible ⁠new treatments of diseases such as cancer. Nobel laureates are chosen by expert committees appointed by the prize-awarding institutions. The awards are presented in Stockholm, with the exception of the Peace Prize, which is handed out in Oslo, a tradition often linked to the union that bound Sweden and Norway during Nobel’s lifetime. More than 125 years after ⁠Nobel signed his ​will, the prizes retain many of their longstanding traditions. The celebrations culminate on December 10, the ​anniversary of Nobel’s death, when laureates receive their awards in ceremonies attended by Sweden’s and Norway’s royal families and are feted at gala banquets held in their honour.

Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO. A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement will be held on Monday in Riyadh and will focus on regional developments and ongoing cooperation among the member states, the Foreign Office (FO) confirmed. In a statement on social media platform X, the FO said Pakistan’s delegation to the meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) will include Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif. “The meeting will also be attended by the respective ministers of foreign affairs, ministers of defence, as well as chiefs of general staff of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and the Republic of Türkiye,” FO added. It said that the member states will discuss “latest developments in the region and review ongoing cooperation under the framework of the Makkah Agreement”. The FO added that Pakistan’s participation signified its “resolve to continue contributing towards regional peace and stability”. In another post, the FO said Dar arrived in Riyadh for the meeting and was received by Major General Othman Al-Zahrani of the Saudi military and Pakistan’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Ahmad Farooq. An earlier post said Dar had arrived in Madina ahead of the meeting, where he paid his respects at the Prophet’s (PBUH) Mosque and offered prayers. Last week, Dar confirmed the meeting while addressing a press briefing. He said the “emergency meeting” would focus on recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The development comes as Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition government launched a major military campaign on Sunday to recapture territory held by the Houthis. Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis showed no signs of abating over the weekend, with the Houthis saying the kingdom had launched dozens of strikes on Yemen’s capital Sanaa, after which they attacked an Aramco facility with ballistic missiles and drones south of Riyadh. The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandeb strait in a lightning offensive. Meanwhile, the defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. The first meeting of the SPDC was held in Istanbul on Aug 31 , during which it was decided that the alliance’s secretariat will be initially headed by Pakistan for three years. Retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood has been appointed as the first secretary general of the alliance. On Sept 25, the military chiefs of Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia met in Riyadh for urgently convened talks under the pact in light of the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. On Sept 18, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry had expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, saying Pakistan will go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”. Defence minister Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan would “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalated.

Hundreds of French high schools shut as protests persist. Lessons were suspended at hundreds of French high schools on Monday, as part of a wave of student protests over learning conditions that have rocked the European nation. Students trickled into some schools despite ongoing protests outside their gates, ahead of a day of larger demonstrations expected on Tuesday. Since late September, pupils have barred the entrances to their schools, complaining of teacher absences, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings ill-adapted to rising temperatures, among other grievances. The government has sought to address the grievances, while accusing hard-left activists of having hijacked the protest movement. Up to 500 out of France’s 3,700 high schools, known as lycees, were expected to be partially or totally closed on Monday, Education Minister Edouard Geffray said late Sunday. A third of the 468 lycees for teenagers aged 15 to 17 were to be closed in the Paris region, authorities said. In the capital’s central third district on Monday morning, dozens of teenage students chanted in protest, as cars honked their horns in support while driving past, while others made their way into class. “No means, no silence,” read one cardboard sign outside the Turgot high school. “We’re missing our lessons to give you one,” read another. A pupil holds a placard reading “To arms, citizens” as protesting students carry out a blockading action at the Turgot secondary school, in Paris, on October 5, 2026. — AFP In the western city of Rennes, more than 20 pupils gathered outside the Montaigne lycee, one clutching a sign that read “Not enough teachers”, but staff allowed other students into their classrooms. In the northern city of Lille, masked protesters destroyed bus shelters or set fire to dustbins, as police fired teargas towards several hundred demonstrators. The movement started on September 17 at a high school in the Paris suburb of Creteil, in support of teachers striking over a lack of staff and resources. It gained momentum and spread across France, at times spiralling into vandalism, including the destruction of bus shelters, the burning of school entrances and clashes between protesters and security forces. Thousands arrested Since the start of the movement, 24 schools had been “burned or ransacked”, according to the education minister. More than 5,000 people, 85 per cent of them minors, have been arrested. Protesters have also accused the police of using disproportionate force, and internal investigations have been opened into at least three instances of alleged police brutality. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu set out a timetable on Sunday urging local authorities to prioritise filling gaps left by long-term teacher absences and unfilled posts. He called a meeting for Tuesday with regional presidents to discuss overhauling the country’s often-dilapidated school buildings. The government is also hoping to pass through parliament a bill to make those who are responsible for damaging public property pay for repairs themselves, instead of drawing from taxpayer money. Government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon defended the bill. “When you have 14-, 15-, 16-year-olds who, at 9 am, are burning bus shelters or — perhaps even more seriously – the high school where they study, that raises the question of parental responsibility,” she told Europe1/Cnews broadcaster. Lecornu has said the draft law, first presented before the protests, would allow these sums to be “taken from family allowances and housing benefits, while ensuring a minimum income is preserved”. The head of the main CGT labour union, Sophie Binet, slammed what she called a “populist announcement”, which she said would “end up targeting the most vulnerable families”.

Bilawal challenges 'system has failed' narrative, cites Tharparkar’s development. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Monday rejected claims that the country’s system had collapsed, saying the development of Tharparkar demonstrated its success. Addressing a ceremony in Tharparkar to inaugurate Phase III of the Thar Coal Project’s Block II, Bilawal said the district’s development was an “archetype of the success” of the country’s system, the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment. He argued that those who claimed the system had collapsed should hand Islamabad over to the people of Tharparkar. Criticising calls for the creation of new provinces and claims that the country’s system had collapsed, Bilawal said: “I don’t get this logic at all, but if we accept it for a moment, it means that Islamabad has failed. Hand Islamabad over to the people of Tharparkar; they will fix it.” Without naming anyone, he said a political party comprising “political orphans” was “busy doing politics of hate, division and Zionism in Karachi”. “I want to tell them that we will never let them succeed,” he said. He said the development achieved in Tharparkar demonstrated the effectiveness of the country’s system and the 18th Constitutional Amendment. “The students of Islamabad can also top all the exams. We have seen the condition of its hospitals; we can make them free and upgrade them to international standards,” he said, taking a dig at the federal government. Bilawal said the progress he had witnessed in the region was unmatched elsewhere in Pakistan. “Not only have its infrastructure, health and education systems improved, but there has been progress in all aspects rather than just changes.” He said Thar’s development had surprised people across the country. “People are unable to digest its development.” Bilawal suggested that Islamabad should follow Tharparkar’s example and also hailed the development achieved in the district through the public-private partnership model. “Today, Thar is generating 14 per cent of the national grid’s electricity and also the cheapest.” He criticised experts in Islamabad who had previously claimed that Thar’s coal was useless and that investing in it would be futile. “Today we are saving up to $1.6 billion of Pakistan’s foreign reserves due to the Thar Coal Project.” The PPP chairman further said the project had also created significant employment opportunities for people in Sindh, noting that “94 per cent of employees of this project belong to Sindh, and 60pc of them hail from Thar district”. ‘Phase III to increase Thar coal mine’s production capacity’ Addressing the ceremony, Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah said the production capacity of the Thar coal mine would increase from 7.6 million tonnes to 11.2m tonnes annually following the completion of Phase III of Thar Block II. “Phase III of Thar Block II will increase the mine’s production capacity by 3.6 million tonnes annually,” he said, adding that the project was being completed with 100pc self-financing. “Electricity generated from Sindh’s local coal will be three times cheaper than electricity generated from imported coal.” He added that Phase III would enable Lucky Electric’s 660-megawatt power plant to operate on Thar coal. “After Phase III, total electricity generation from Thar will reach 1,980 megawatts.” The chief minister also said 4.5m households would benefit from electricity generated from Thar every day following the completion of Phase III. “Phase III will result in annual savings of approximately Rs15 billion in electricity generation costs,” he said, adding that the project would save Pakistan approximately $220m annually in additional foreign exchange. He said Phase III would also pave the way for the launch of Thar Rail. “The launch of Thar Rail will make Thar coal accessible across the country.” Shah said the Thar Coal Project was an important example of public-private partnership in Pakistan’s mining sector.

Remaining 3 Pakistanis rescued from hijacked vessel in Somalia expected to fly home on Wednesday. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Monday that the three remaining Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25, an oil tanker that was hijacked off the coast of Somalia in April, are expected to be flown back to Pakistan on Wednesday. The maritime police force of Somalia’s semi-autonomous Puntland said last week that it had recovered the MT Honour 25 , a Palau-flagged oil tanker with 19 crew members on board, including 10 Pakistanis, which had been hijacked by Somali pirates in April. The Foreign Office subsequently confirmed that three Pakistanis had died and several others were injured during the operation, later identifying the deceased as Rafiullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmed Ansari. Four Pakistanis injured in the operation had arrived in Karachi on Sunday, with the remains of those killed. In a post on the social media platform X, Dar said three crew members, Imran Ali, Muhammad Yasin and Syed Husain Yousuf, have been “successfully rescued” and flown to Addis Ababa — the capital of Ethiopia — accompanied by a team from the Pakistan embassy in Djibouti. “The three crew members will be received in Addis Ababa and depart for Pakistan on the first available Ethiopian Airlines flight to Karachi,” Dar said, adding that this flight would be expected on Oct 7 (Wednesday). He expressed his gratitude to the government of Somalia and the European Union Naval Force Operation Atalanta for their assistance and cooperation in securing the crew’s release. “Pakistan remains firmly committed to strengthening bilateral and multilateral cooperation to combat maritime piracy and safeguard the security and freedom of international maritime routes,” he added. Apart from Pakistanis, the vessel’s crew also included seven Indonesians, an Indian and a Sri Lankan. After the hijacking, months passed with no progress either in negotiations or the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages. The hostages were said to be victims of an “ ownership crisis ”, as it was not clearly established who owned the ship — the man previously thought to be an owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them. Since its hijacking, the crew had made several emotional videos and audio appeals , reporting that they had run out of clean water, food and medicine. Meanwhile, their families launched an international appeal, calling on foreign governments, the United Nations (UN) and the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) to take coordinated action to help secure the release of their loved ones. For its part, FO maintained that it remained “actively engaged” to secure the release of the sailors. On Sept 29, Somali maritime police recovered the Palau-flagged oil tanker amid reports of casualties among the crew. During the operation, it said, 21 suspected pirates were apprehended, while operations to locate the remaining members continue.

‘Abandoned province’: Amir Muqam slams PTI, says not in favour of governor’s rule in KP but security risks persist. Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam on Monday slammed the PTI-led government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, stressing that the federal government was not “in favour of governor’s rule” amid the party’s march, but warning of national security risks. The minister’s comments came as KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi launched the party’s long march towards Islamabad on Sunday, saying that the party would “not accept” any policy against the interests of the people of KP. PTI went ahead with its march despite warnings from the federal government. The government has threatened to send the PTI government in KP packing by imposing governor’s rule or an emergency if the party proceeded with the march. The march was announced as part of its nationwide protest to demand the release of its founder, Imran Khan. It has become a major bone of contention between the government and the main opposition party, with both taking entrenched positions. Addressing a press conference on Monday, Muqam said, “We are not in favour of having governor’s rule or declaring an emergency in KP as politically it is not a good decision; however, on the one hand, you have politicians, and then there is the state. Politics can only continue if we still have control of the province.” He claimed that the provincial government had lost its writ and that “the security situation was deteriorating day by day”. Speaking about the recent negotiations with the opposition over the party’s march to Islamabad, the minister said the government’s side had suggested that they “be on the same page” about terrorism. Muqam said the province’s chief executive had “abandoned” the province. “There is no sign of the government in the province. The chief executive of the province stays busy with his one-point agenda.” He said terrorism was not limited to KP. Muqam went on to warn, “If KP is overtaken by terrorists [..] then the rest of Pakistan would not remain free either.” He said the provincial government, the federal government and the armed forces “should be on the same page” in counterterrorism efforts. Shifting his attention to the weekend’s negotiations with the opposition, Muqam applauded the opposition’s delegation, saying that they were willing to find a resolution. He recalled that during the first day of the talks, the opposition asked for an extension since the KP CM needed to be a part as well. “The next day, we came back and sat from 3pm till 3am. In the talks, three to four drafts were prepared, and at one point, it was decided that we would issue a joint statement.” He said that at the time, the opposition’s delegation had assured the government side of their cooperation. He recalled that the “interference” began after 9pm on Saturday. “Messages came in asking for clauses to be added and removed. In the end, we had a deadlock,” Muqam said. The minister said it was “highly unfortunate” that the talks had ended. He also questioned how the KP CM was making statements regarding the march while “his nominated people were engaging in talks”. He claimed that government-related work in KP had come to a halt over the past two to two-and-a-half months. Muqam reiterated that the federal and provincial governments “needed to be on the same page”. He also questioned the provincial government’s “lack of seriousness” over the National Action Plan (NAP). “Why have you held only one meeting in the entire year? How many martyrs have you visited?” Muqam asked. “In fact, you went against the police to try to rob them of their authority,” he said, referring to the KP Police Act, 2026. During his press conference, Muqam reiterated that PTI’s march would not be allowed to enter Islamabad. “What is this drama of proceeding with the march when you know fully well that you will not be allowed to enter Punjab?” Muqam said to PTI. He questioned whether the KP government had spoken about the rights of the people of KP. “It is the state’s responsibility not to leave the people of KP at the mercy of terrorists, and for that, there is a constitutional way to provide them relief,” the minister said, in an apparent reference to governor’s rule. Asked about further negotiations with the opposition, the minister said the “door to talks is still open [..] if it is for the betterment of the country, we are always ready to talk”. ‘Terrorism, not politics, is the problem’ Separately, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif also emphasised the gravity of the security situation in KP and appeared to be holding the PTI’s provincial government responsible for the prevalent terrorism. “The state and KP’s problem is not politics but terrorism,” he began in a post on X before sharing terrorism-related data. According to Asif, around 6,200 terrorism incidents took place in the province over the past two years, 1,200 personnel were martyred and 37 suicide attacks by Afghans were recorded. “Fourteen suicide attacks have taken place in the ongoing year, most of which have the involvement of Afghans.” Moving on to law enforcement agencies, he said the total number of police personnel in KP was 125,000 and 13,000 among them were deployed for VIP protocol. On the other hand, he said, 17,000 police posts remained vacant “in a province where police are playing an important role [against] terrorism”. He went on to allege that the “Counterterrorism Department’s (CTD) system is nearly non-functional in the merged districts”. According to Asif, the department had just 17 bulletproof vehicles and the total number of CTD personnel was around 3,300. Among them, only 25 were permanent employees and rest were contract-based employees, he said. The defence minister then accused the government of trying to undermine the police’s capacity by “using the Police Act 2017 for political purposes”. He further alleged that police had sought funds worth Rs42 billion for the reconstruction of police posts, but the provincial government released just Rs1.2bn. “Lives are being lost every day due to the non-provision of funds. On the other hand, expenditure of Rs42bn has been claimed in papers, when in reality, this amount has been embezzled,” he said. In this scenario, Asif said, the PTI’s stance had been that if security forces had been guarding the frontiers, then how were terrorists able to infiltrate into the country. Noting that the PTI had been in the government in KP for the past 13 years, he alleged that “Imran had a soft spot for the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP)” — an outlawed terror outfit — and the PTI’s view had been more inclined towards holding talks with terrorists. He accused Imran of “pushing the entire security system towards talks with the TTP and its allied groups”. “Pakistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa paid the price for this policy,” he regretted. “Yet, this party (PTI) is talking about engaging the TTP and TTA (Tehreek-i-Taliban Afghan) today.” The defence minister asserted that the state had a clear policy on terrorism now. “The state’s policy is to not hold talks with terrorists but to take action against them.” Asif said the KP government’s policy was contrary to the state’s policy. He said there had been accusations that the fight against terrorism was for “dollars”. “Tell us, how many billions of dollars has America provided to Pakistan in the past few years for the fight against terrorism and security?” he questioned. “Tell us, are the drone strikes in Kohat and Peshawar and the TTA attacks on Pakistani security posts not real? When terrorists themselves are using drones, why can’t the army use drones for its own defence?” Raising several questions regarding counterterrorism measures taken by the PTI, he also refuted the KP government’s allegation that they were not being provided funds by the Centre. “There is no lack of funds, but corruption and weak governance diminish their impact,” he claimed. The defence minister went on to say, after claiming funds transfers to KP on several accounts, that “the number of pending prosecution cases is approximately 3,000, but no terrorist has been executed yet, nor has any punishment been awarded”. He said the state’s clear policy was “hold, build and transfer”. “First secure and hold the areas, then begin reconstruction and build an institutional structure and then transfer [the control] to the civil administration,” he elaborated. “The question is why are you not applying the policy of hold, build and transfer in these areas? Your judiciary and civil administration should step forward to take charge of managing these areas,” he concluded. Opp-govt dialogue failure Over the weekend, the government and opposition held two rounds of talks , which did not yield positive results, with counterterrorism policies and access to Imran emerging as two major sticking points. On Sunday, the PTI said it wanted immediate access to party chief Imran for consultations, and even agreed to forgo other demands in return for a meeting with Imran. However, the government declined to make access to Imran part of the proposed agreement, the opposition party claimed. Another deadlock was terrorism in KP. The federal government asked the KP government to support its counterterrorism measures and support emergency measures within 72 hours in the merged tribal districts, the PTI said. Instead, the PTI proposed that authorised representatives of the federal and KP governments meet within 72 hours to develop a clear, comprehensive and mutually agreed strategy for peace and counterterrorism, the statement added. The PTI said the health and medical treatment of Imran Khan was also raised as a matter of fundamental importance. Meanwhile, PTI leader Salman Akram Raja, who was a part of the opposition’s delegation, said the primary reason for the failure was disagreement on anti-terrorism actions in KP. Raja said the opposition stood firm on its principled position that anti-terrorism actions should be based on an agreement between the federal government and the KP government, and would be framed in consultation with stakeholders. After talks between the government and the opposition ended without headway, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday accused CM Afridi of “sabotaging” negotiations. On Sunday, Naqvi also held a meeting with the KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi to discuss the political and security situation amid speculations of ‘imminent’ governor’s rule in the province. A government source told Dawn that the government was seriously considering the imposition of the governor’s rule in KP.

After breakdown of talks with govt, PTI says reconciliation not possible without including Imran. ISLAMABAD: PTI leaders on Monday declared that reconciliation between their party and the government was not possible without including incarcerated party founder Imran Khan in the dialogue process. Narrating the opposition’s stance on why the talks with the government failed over the weekend, PTI’s secretary general, Salman Akram Raja, presented his party’s demand that Imran be included in any future political dialogue. “Only [Imran] has the capability to bridge the gulf that has developed between the state and the nation,” Raja said during the press conference held at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa House in Islamabad. “Imran Khan is very important for us and we had every right to seek his opinion, but it was not allowed,” Raja said. The PTI leader said that another reason for the failure of the talks was that the government was not willing to pursue a collective strategy against terrorism. Raja told the media that the PTI had entered into the negotiations with sincerity and was serious about addressing the issues. “Even on the second day, we were hoping that another round of talks would streamline things,” he said. Describing the reasons for talks failing, Raja said: “We were being pushed to support the government over every action being taken regarding terrorism in KP.” He added that the PTI had demanded that the government respect the recommendations and opinions of a jirga held by the KP Assembly, in which political parties and stakeholders had participated. The jirga had recommended solutions to the problem, the opposition delegation had told the government, according to Raja. The delegation had also asked the government to consider the opinions of tribal leaders, Raja said. He said the PTI had suggested the agreement should mention that a collective decision would be made regarding terrorism, but the government had said it would not put it down on paper. “We were told that a unanimous strategy against terrorism would not be developed and it would not be included in the agreement,” he said. Raja said that the government had deliberately complicated the situation. “It is a fact that the current issues can only be addressed by Imran Khan. “We had demanded that Imran Khan and his opinion should be included in all issues, which is why we demanded a meeting of party leaders with him,” Raja said. The two rounds of talks between the government and the opposition held on Friday and Saturday did not yield positive results, with counterterrorism policies and access to Imran emerging as two major sticking points. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who was part of the process, on Sunday singled out KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi for the failure of talks, saying that he changed the agreement. Separately, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the PTI representatives came for talks but were unwilling to abandon their “double standards and hypocrisy”. For its part, the PTI said it wanted immediate access to party founder Imran for consultations, and even agreed to forgo other demands for this. However, the government declined to make access to Imran part of the proposed agreement, the opposition party claimed. Addressing the failed talks, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam said on Monday that the government’s delegation had suggested that both sides “be on the same page” about terrorism. Following the failed talks, the PTI went ahead with its protest march on Sunday despite warnings from the federal government. KP Assembly speaker to summon security committee meeting Against this backdrop, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Swati said he was going to summon another meeting of a special committee on security, which was constituted after a peace jirga in the assembly in November last year. “I am again summoning a meeting of the special committee. I wish for the relevant authorities and institutions to sit together on this important matter,” he posted on X. He emphasised that it was important to consider this process initiated by the KP Assembly before the Centre held the former responsible for the law and order situation in the province. Swati recalled that political parties had issued a joint statement after the Nov peace jirga, in light of which the assembly had constituted a special committee on security. The committee, he said, was briefed by the provincial police chief, the Counterterrorism Department, the KP home additional chief secretary, the Home Department, the KP chief secretary and other relevant provincial institutions. “We also informed the leadership in the Centre about this process and sent letters to the prime minister, the Senate chairman, the National Assembly speaker and the interior minister, informing them that the assembly was moving towards [formulating] comprehensive parliamentary recommendations,” he said. Swati said just one important official, the Peshawar corps commander, was left to brief the committee. “I had spoken to the Peshawar corps commander and he had assured me of his participation. However, the meeting has yet to take place,” he added. “I am again summoning a meeting of the special committee. I wish for the relevant authorities and institutions to sit together on this important matter. “Whatever we have heard, seen, and whatever facts have come before the committee — they will present their stance; the relevant institutions will present theirs,” Swati said. Following that, he continued, the committee would formulate its recommendations, which would be presented before the assembly. “After the assembly’s approval, the recommendations will be forwarded to the provincial and federal governments so that responsibility, policy and practical measures are clearly [stated].” The speaker said the people of KP wanted peace and called for the relevant parties to play their respective roles in moving towards a collective solution. “We have to find a way while collectively implementing the National Action Plan, clarifying the responsibilities of relevant institutions,” he added.

ECP 'ready' for LG polls in Punjab but cites legal and administrative hurdles in KP, Islamabad. ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Monday said it was ready to hold local government (LG) elections in Punjab but faces legal and administrative hurdles in conducting polls in Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Quetta and cantonment boards. The assessment came at a special meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja to review preparations for LG polls in all provinces, Islamabad and cantonments. According to a statement by the ECP, the commission was briefed on province-wise progress on the exercise. On Punjab, the meeting was informed that the ECP was prepared to hold LG polls and had sent a draft election schedule to the provincial government. The ECP has sought lists for appointment of district returning officers, returning officers and assistant returning officers to enable appointments, and also asked the Punjab government to respond to the draft schedule at the earliest. ECP further said that the preparations had been started in Sindh for timely holding of local body polls and instructions had been issued to its office to take all necessary steps. Legal issues in capital, cantts In Islamabad, delimitation had been completed, but the Islamabad Capital Territory Amendment Ordinance 2026 had lapsed , the meeting was informed. According to the statement, a National Assembly Standing Committee had approved legislation in line with the ordinance and therefore, the ECP decided to take up the matter with the federal government for the “immediate completion of legislation”. If legislation was not done, the ECP said it would proceed to hold elections under the existing Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act 2015. On the local body polls in the cantonments, the meeting was briefed that delimitation in all cantonments had been completed and the ECP was ready to hold polls. However, under Section 19-D of the amended Cantonments Act, the federal government was required to make a formal request to the ECP for holding elections. “Despite reminders and a letter from the chief election commissioner to the prime minister, no request had been received,” the statement said. It added: “The ECP decided to write a final letter to the Ministry of Defence, failing which it would take an appropriate decision regarding holding of elections.” KP delimitation On Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the ECP recalled that delimitation had been completed in 23 districts and was underway in seven when the provincial government amended Section 6 of the KP Local Government Act 2013, raising the threshold for village and neighbourhood councils from 5,000-15,000 to 30,000-40,000. The ECP noted the amended threshold was not in conformity with the number of village and neighbourhood councils given in the 9th Schedule of the Act, making delimitation unworkable. According to the statement, the provincial government had been asked to assist the ECP and suitably amend the number of councils in the 9th Schedule. With no action taken, the case was under hearing before the ECP, which would take an “appropriate decision”. ‘Slow’ response from Balochistan govt Regarding Balochistan, the statement said the term of LG institutions will expire on Feb 8, 2027. However, it noted that LG polls in Quetta could not be held despite orders of the Federal Constitutional Court. The ECP said it had completed delimitation on May 21, 2026, in compliance with the court order, but the provincial government bifurcated Quetta into two districts without providing boundary details and other data. The commission went on to observe that the Balochistan government’s response regarding this was “really slow”. The ECP decided to write to the provincial government for early completion of legislation and compliance with the court order, it stated. ECP members Nisar Ahmed Durrani, Shah Mohammad Jatoi and Justice (retired) Ikramullah, along with ECP Secretary Omar Hamid and other senior officers, attended the meeting.

US withdraws all bomber aircraft from UK airbase used during Iran war. The United States confirmed that it had withdrawn all B-1 bombers from the British airbase of RAF Fairford, reportedly due to “new threats”, with Britain’s government insisting on Monday that the site is safe. Police were called to the base in southwest England on Sept 27 after a local farmer reported a group of men with several vans engaged in “suspicious” activity. The scare prompted a counter-terrorism probe and forced evacuations at 85 homes near the airbase, which was used by the US to launch strikes on Iran. Investigators did not find any explosives in the vans, but “a quantity of petrol was recovered”, according to counter-terrorism police. A statement from a Pentagon official on Sunday said, “We can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have redeployed to their home stations in the United States.” The statement noted that “operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time”. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Monday expressed “confidence in the security of all of our bases”. US facilities “theoretically could be threatened at any moment, and that’s why there’s so much security built around them”, Rubio said, adding that Washington had worked with London on the investigation and “they couldn’t be more cooperative”. An unidentified US official told CNN that the bombers were moved after “an unspecified new threat”, with the source calling the latest threat a “real world incident”. It was unusual to move the bombers back to their home stations instead of deploying them to another base in the region, the official reportedly said. Two US officials told the New York Times that the bombers were moved after commanders received new threats about an alleged Iran-backed plot against the base. One American official said the new information was part of the same threat warnings that surfaced three weeks ago, but the situation became urgent in the past 24 hours, NYT reported. Asked whether the base was safe, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s official spokesman said: “Yes.” “We have tried and tested approaches to defend our bases around the country and throughout the world,” he told reporters. Heightened security Speculation about the motives behind the incident ranged from terror threat to fuel theft, as energy prices in the UK hit record highs this week. Burnham has said there were “strong indications that Iran played a part” in the incident, a charge rejected by Tehran . Six London-based Britons arrested in the September incident, including a UK-Iranian dual national , all men in their mid-20s, were released on bail , drawing rebuke from Washington. “I wouldn’t have done that,” US President Donald Trump told reporters, while Rubio alleged a “foreign actor” was involved. View this post on Instagram Iran’s embassy in London said it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” speculation that Tehran was involved. Adding to the mystery, British media reported that officers were alerted to the incident by one of the initial suspects, but police have not commented on the reports. Security at the base had reportedly been heightened recently. Britain gave Washington permission in March to use Fairford for “specific defensive operations into Iran”, and US bombers and other planes have since been seen taking off and landing at the base. Fairford is the only airbase on Britain’s mainland used for this purpose. The incident came after a farmer living in the village of Whelford, near the airbase, called the police after seeing three vans blocking a road and a group of masked men fleeing the scene. Aerial footage of the vans showed they appeared to contain barrels, and at least one was marked with a fake logo and phone number, giving the false impression that it was owned by a legitimate diesel delivery firm.

PTI long march: After Karak address, KP CM's convoy departs for Kohat. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday resumed PTI’s march as he addressed supporters in Karak, from where his convoy will depart for Kohat. The opposition has gone ahead with its march despite warnings from the Centre, which has vowed to prevent any gatherings in Islamabad. The protest aims to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan. PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government to bridge their differences failed for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy. As per an update by PTI after 6pm on Monday, the Afridi-led march was advancing from Karak towards Kohat. Addressing party supporters at Karak’s Jail Chowk in the afternoon, the chief minister again railed against the Centre’s counterterrorism policy and criticised past military operations and drone attacks. Afridi also referred to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s remarks from a day earlier, wherein the latter called him “immature”. He went on to recall Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz’s remarks on the terrorism threat to her province, adding: “Suppose, I say that [my province] does not have a threat from India, but from the other three provinces, will you consider me mature?” The KP CM said, “If you deem it immature to speak about one’s province and people, then I have shown this immaturity yesterday, still do and will keep doing so.” Afridi contended that “wrong policies drafted behind closed doors were impacting all institutions”. Expressing his patriotism for Pakistan, the PTI leader said, “We also chant Pakistan zindabad , we stand up for the national anthem as well.” But he added that future generations might not do so as there were attempts to “divide Pakistan and spread hatred”. Insisting that his party was democratically presenting the public’s demands, Afridi warned that if the situation crossed all limits, neither would he be able to control the public “nor will anyone’s father have the courage” to do so. He asserted that only those policies would be implemented that the people and the youth desire, and which were in the interests of the nation. “We will not accept any decision taken behind closed doors that is against us, our province or Pakistan,” the KP CM added. He argued that Imran could secure his release if he wanted but was choosing to remain behind bars for the nation’s “freedom”. “He is free even in jail, and we are slaves even when free,” he quipped. The chief minister urged people to reach Swabi, adding that no one could even imagine or think of the next plan of action. Earlier, Afridi’s focal person for digital media Yar Muhammad Khan Niazi shared a video on X of PTI supporters welcoming the KP CM at Karak’s Jail Chowk. According to a post by CM Afridi, the people of Karak were to join the convoy at 12pm, with the departure set for 12:30pm, which faced a delay. The convoy plans to stay overnight in Kohat, and then resume the journey towards Peshawar at noon on Oct 6. It will spend the night near Mattani. On the afternoon of Oct 7, the caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar and spend the night near Charsadda Interchange. The protesters will then move forward the next afternoon and spend the night of Oct 8 at Khairabad. Notably, the KP CM has refrained from detailing the final leg of the trip to the federal capital and said the plan for the next phase would be announced at Khairabad. This screengrab from Google Maps shows the planned route of the PTI convoy from Lakki Marwat to Khairabad, where it is scheduled to reach on Oct 8. The march so far After launching the already-postponed march from Lakki Marwat on Sunday afternoon, the KP CM’s caravan reached Karak at night, where Afridi addressed supporters at Jail Chowk. Ahead of the march, movement on several roads in KP’s Dera Ismail Khan, Upper and Lower South Waziristan, Tank and Hangu was restricted under Section 144 for varying periods . On Monday, former KP CM Ali Amin Gandapur, who was leading PTI workers from DI Khan to Lakki Marwat, took a U-turn from Yarik because of road blockades and the prevailing law and order situation. Noting that Section 144 had been imposed in the area for three days, Gandapur stressed that the party leadership had clearly directed workers not to damage public property or engage in any activity that could worsen the situation. Nevertheless, he contended that the return should not be viewed as a withdrawal from the protest movement, but as a temporary decision. In Karachi , a planned protest campaign in different areas was disrupted after police deployed personnel at several locations, blocked roads and detained several party workers and leaders. The PTI claimed that police detained more than 75 of its leaders and workers, including women, from different parts of Karachi. It further alleged that arrests made in other parts of Sindh, including Sukkur, put the total number of detained PTI workers across the province at more than 100. On Saturday night, an opposition delegation comprising PTI and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), and a joint team of the government and PPP held hours-long negotiations , which ended in a deadlock. While the federal government blamed CM Afridi for the failure of negotiations, PTI denied the allegations and claimed that access to Imran, his medical treatment and the federal government’s counterterrorism policy were the key reasons. According to PTI, the government agreed to restore meetings between Imran and his family members and lawyers from Tuesday, but “declined to make access to Imran Khan part of the proposed agreement”.

Upper parts of country likely to see rainy, windy conditions from Oct 6-7. The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) on Monday predicted heavy rains, strong winds and thunderstorms, with isolated hailstorms, in the upper parts of the country over the next two days. In a press release, the Met Office said a westerly wave was likely to enter the upper parts of the country tonight and was expected to persist until Oct 7 (Wednesday). Under the influence of this weather system, the PMD predicted rain, windstorms and thunderstorms, with isolated hailstorms, in various locations in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Punjab as well as the Islamabad region. In KP, “rain-windstorm/thunderstorm” were expected to begin from Monday night in Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Shangla, Battagram, Mansehra, Abbottabad, Haripur, Buner, Malakand, Bajaur, Mohmand, Kohat, Peshawar, Charsadda, Nowshera, Mardan, Swabi, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, Hangu, Lakki Marwat, Karak, Bannu, Dera Ismail Khan and Waziristan. They are predicted to last until Oct 7 (Wednesday), the PMD said. In Kashmir, rain and hail were expected to fall during the next two days in isolated places, including Neelum Valley, Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot, Poonch, Hattian, Bagh, Haveli, Sudhanoti, Kotli, Bhimber and Mirpur. In GB, they were likely in Diamer, Astore, Ghizer, Skardu, Hunza, Gilgit, Ghanche and Shigar during the same period. For Punjab, the PMD forecast “rain-windstorm/thunderstorm” on Oct 6 and Oct 7 at isolated places in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Murree, Galliyat, Attock, Chakwal, Jhelum, Mandi Bahauddin, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad, Lahore, Kasur, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Narowal, Mianwali, Khushab, Sargodha, Jhang, Toba Tek Singh and Faisalabad. While “mainly hot and dry weather” was likely to prevail in Sindh and Balochistan, the PMD noted that rain-windstorms and thunderstorms were also expected at isolated places in Balochistan’s Zhob, Barkhan and Musakhel on Tuesday evening and night. The Met Office warned that windstorms, hail and lightning could damage weak structures such as roofs and walls of kutcha houses, electric poles, billboards, vehicles and solar panels. It also noted that daytime temperatures were likely to drop by two to four degrees Celsius during the forecast period. “Farmers are advised to manage their crop activities keeping in view the weather conditions,” the press release stated, also calling on all relevant authorities to remain vigilant and take the necessary measures to avoid untoward situations. A fresh spell of rain hit the country last month, particularly affecting Rawalpindi as inundated roads and knee-deep water at certain points exposed the city’s poor drainage system. Islamabad and Rawalpindi received another burst of heavy rain at the end of September, with civic departments in the garrison city placed on high alert. Earlier that month, KP also witnessed rain as heavy downpours lashed Mohmand, damaging and flooding roads and creating difficulties for residents. Rain coupled with strong winds and dust had also damaged vegetable and maize crops in Bajaur district, but no casualties were reported.

Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Multilateral Diplomacy In this episode of Hold Your Fire! , Richard Atwood speaks with Richard Gowan, Crisis Group’s Director for Global Issues and Institutions, and Daniel Forti, Head of UN affairs, ahead of next week’s UN General Assembly high-level week. They explore the mood at the UN, its shifting relations with Washington and its shrinking role in peacemaking worldwide, particularly in the Middle East. They assess current Secretary-General António Guterres’s legacy, the contenders to succeed him and whether new leadership can reinvigorate the organisation’s peacemaking while defending the UN Charter’s principles and rebuilding relationships with powerful states.
